decisions.reason: It remained prominently presented through 2019 and fits the firm's core application-technology business, so performance likely stayed near aspiration levels and a medium-sized established firm would usually keep such a related niche product unless stronger evidence of underperformance emerged.

Its continued standalone presentation in 2019 suggests acceptable early results, and because it uses the firm's existing engineering, production and sales resources, management would likely retain it while returns are at least satisfactory enough.

An automatic airless spray gun is highly aligned with the firm's established spray-equipment portfolio, so boundedly rational management would be inclined to continue it when no clear sign of failure below aspiration is visible.

A manual airless spray gun sits squarely in the firm's core product family and service network, making it relatively easy to support with existing slack and therefore less likely to be dropped absent clear poor results.

As a multi-model product line in a central technology area, it signals stronger commitment and broader market coverage, which makes continued retention most likely unless performance were clearly far below aspirations.

The shift from a dedicated page in 2018 to only a mention in 2019 suggests weaker traction, and because this data logger is more peripheral than the firm's core mechanical equipment, management would be more likely to reallocate resources away from it after unsatisfactory results.
